knowledge:
- key_parameters: <exprs=A normalized gene expression matrix (log2 scale, e.g., RMA normalized) where rows represent genes and columns represent samples. Can contain NA values for missing data ;; groupid=A vector identifying the group/condition label of each sample ;; compgroup=A matrix representing the study design and comparison pattern, where columns represent conditions to compare and rows represent studies ;; K=A vector of motif numbers to fit (e.g., 1:5) to select the best model using AIC/BIC ;; max.iter=Maximum number of iterations for the EM algorithm ;; BIC=Logical indicating whether to calculate BIC (and AIC) for model selection>
- alternatives: <cormotiffitall=Fits a model assuming genes are either differentially expressed in all studies or none (concordance model); use when studies are expected to be completely concordant ;; cormotiffitsep=Fits the mixture model to each study separately; use when studies are completely independent and do not share information ;; cormotiffitfull=Fits all 2^D possible 0-1 motif patterns; use when the number of studies D is very small and full representation is computationally feasible>
- when_to_use: <When analyzing multiple transcriptomics studies addressing the same biological problem to detect study-specific and shared differential expression patterns, especially when datasets have missing values or non-overlapping genes due to different platforms.>
- pitfalls: <Input expression data must be normalized (e.g., log2 scale) before running the model. Using cormotiffitfull with a large number of studies will lead to exponential growth of the parameter space and high computational cost.>

workflows.name: correlation_motif_analysis
workflows.intent: Fit correlation motif models to multiple gene expression studies to identify shared and study-specific differential expression patterns, handle missing data, and rank genes.
input: exprs.simu2 (matrix of normalized gene expression values)
workflows.stages:
1. Prepare expression matrix, group IDs, and comparison group matrix.
2. Fit correlation motif models for a range of motif numbers (K) using cormotiffit.
3. Evaluate model fit using BIC/AIC values and plot information criteria using plotIC.
4. Visualize the discovered correlation motifs and their frequencies using plotMotif.
5. Extract posterior probabilities of differential expression and identify active patterns.
6. Rank genes in each study based on posterior probabilities using generank.
7. (Optional) Fit alternative models (all, separate, or full motifs) using cormotiffitall, cormotiffitsep, or cormotiffitfull.
workflows.code:
library(Cormotif)
data(simudata2)
colnames(simudata2)
exprs.simu2<-as.matrix(simudata2[,2:25])
data(simu2_groupid)
simu2_groupid
data(simu2_compgroup)
simu2_compgroup
motif.fitted<-cormotiffit(exprs.simu2,simu2_groupid,simu2_compgroup,
			 K=1:5,max.iter=1000,BIC=TRUE)
motif.fitted$bic
plotIC(motif.fitted)
plotMotif(motif.fitted)
head(motif.fitted$bestmotif$p.post)
dif.pattern.simu2<-(motif.fitted$bestmotif$p.post>0.5)
head(dif.pattern.simu2)
topgenelist<-generank(motif.fitted$bestmotif$p.post)
head(topgenelist)
motif.fitted.all<-cormotiffitall(exprs.simu2,simu2_groupid,simu2_compgroup,max.iter=1)
motif.fitted.sep<-cormotiffitsep(exprs.simu2,simu2_groupid,simu2_compgroup,max.iter=1)
motif.fitted.full<-cormotiffitfull(exprs.simu2,simu2_groupid,simu2_compgroup,max.iter=1)
